content: “ N o,  M istress .  I mean I have heard stories, but you have never talked  about it , ”  he said,  his  excitement barley  contained .   Crandon  had only been riding with Corliss for a few weeks ;  before that he had spent the better part of five years in training and then working with three previous wardens before getting paired with Corliss for his final evaluation.  Uri had told her before she left for this hunt  that  the kid would accompany her .   [Insert who Uri is/his title]  had high hopes for the young man, and it said something as this is the first time that Corliss had been paired with an apprentice.  She just wasn’t sure if it said good things about her , about  the kid ,  or both . Uri was like that ;  he enjoyed throwing curveballs to see  watch peoples reactions .  Sitting back, she regarded the young man, so exuberant and excited about his first hunt.  Though Corliss did not know why the Lord Adjudicator for the  warden s would  send him  out after Castigan .   The criminal  was incredibly  dangerous ,  which  was one of the reasons she had ensured the shop keeper had kept young  Crandon  busy while she was securing the fugitive.  If things had not gone  her way ,  the shopkeeper  would have hidden the young man until more wardens could arrive.  Corliss thanked the gods that wasn’t  necessary .   S he  would need to have a talk with Uri when she got back .   T he poor kid should have been sent on an easier assignment.  She turned to  Crandon.   “I was  younger than  you — probably  about five years  younger ,  which  would have made me twelve — and  m y mother had died of fever and my father had left us  years before .   H e had wanted a son .   S omeone he could leave his legacy to .   B ut instead he was given a bastard .   A  female  one, at that .  “ I fell  in with local gangs in the capital ,  and one day I was picking the pocket of a  brutish - looking  fellow and he caught  me . ” Corliss  smiled ,  remembering  that day well .   I t was the day that changed her life forever and made her what she was today.  “Instead of turning me in, the barbarian  made me his apprentice .   H is name was Uri Ammital .   Y ou know him as the Lord Adjudicator . ”  The young man leaned closer , enraptured by the tale which sh e was sure had been told to him many times .   M ost  young apprentices heard  the tale of Corliss and her misadventures with  her master .  “ He  taught me everything I know .   H e was an amazing teacher ,  and took me under his wing  until the day I took the  vows , ” she  finished still smiling at the thought of  her mentor .  Uri had been more than a teacher ;  he had been like a father to  her  when  she had needed one most .   F ollowing in  his footsteps had been easy .  Corliss had worshipped the man and everything he stood for.  “Uri once told me that one person can make  a difference .   O ne  person can change the course of history should they be brave enough to stand in the way of destiny .” Taking advantage of the break in the tale ,   Crandon  sp oke up .   “Is it true Lord Ammital taught you to be a master brawler and a master swordsman by the time you were sixteen?”   Corliss chuckled.  “I see old Vegram has been telling stories while getting you to work in the  kitchen ,”  Corliss chuckled.   “Yes, it is true . ”  T he young man seemed to be exploding out of his saddle  at this .   “ T hat’s amazing . ”   Corliss waved him off .  “Mastering martial combat is not the hardest thing you will do as  a junior  warden . ” They  rode  in  silence for a while, her faith in Uri and her doubt in the  young  man’s abilities warring with each other .   Corliss had never recalled an initiate being paired with a warden on anything more than a simple courier mission or court  appearance.  Uri  didn’t do anything without a reason and everything he did was meant to test one or both people  involved .   T hat was his way .  “Ghost,”  Crandon  asked tentatively , b reaking the  silence ,  “ h ow hard is it to follow the living oath ?   D o you ever wish you hadn’t taken it?”  Corliss nodded .   T his was a question every initiate eventually asked .   Even she had  asked it of Uri.  “I will first tell you what Lord Ammital told me the first time I asked him that question. The  warden s are the line between anarchy and law in the land, there is no other .   A nd if the  warden s  ceased to be ,  then  the country would descend into throws of lawlessne ss , ”  she  stated ,   remembering  when she had been given this speech.
